study: S2b — same factorial, SEARCH factor restored to S1's original 248-char text
why: S2 found no search effect, and its manipulation check showed the shortened SEARCH sentence did not move measured search (P(score>=2) 17.6% -> 10.0%, i.e. DOWN). S2b substitutes S1's original search text, which under the same rubric nearly doubled it (12.6% -> 24.1%). This separates 'the effect needs that wording/dose' from 'there is no search effect'.
changed_from_S2: ONLY the SEARCH factor text. FRAME, stem, closer, n, seeds policy, outcome and analysis are unchanged.
known_confound_stated_in_advance: SEARCH (248 chars) is now roughly twice the length of FRAME (120 chars), so the cells are not length-matched. This is deliberate: S2 already tested the length-matched version and its manipulation failed. Length is therefore confounded with the search factor here, and the two studies bracket it.
